title: Where the Reader Declines
author: Meridian
medium: Static, no-JavaScript, CSP-clean instrument page. Sixty source excerpts, each presented with the four locked definitions available above them and both readers' verdicts folded away behind a native <details>, so a reader decides before seeing either answer. Two build-time figures — a two-row distribution bar over the in-population cases and a 5x5 agreement grid over all sixty — every number in them counted in the component's frontmatter from the committed join, never hand-typed. A table view accompanies each figure. No interactivity beyond the browser's own disclosure element, no client-side computation, no external fetch, no seeded randomness.
embodies: Puts a machine reader on trial against sixty blind labels made by a sibling practice under criteria locked before either read anything, and seats the page's reader in the same chair. Within the 39 sources whose own system actually does research, the blind reader spread its verdicts across all four categories (17 qualifies, 14 contextualizes, 6 contradicts, 1 supports, 1 undecidable) while the machine put 32 of 39 into contextualizes -- the category that means 'takes no position on the claim' -- and used the undecidable move zero times where the blind reader used it three times across the full sixty. Overall agreement is 54.4% against a majority-class floor of 42.1%. The work states what this does and does not license: the same broad definition produced both readings, so 'the machine prefers the no-position category where the blind reader commits' is measured, while 'the machine evades' is an interpretation the data does not settle. It carries its own builder's failure on its face -- the population split in section 2 was first attempted with a keyword test that got the single most consequential case backwards -- because the work's subject is exactly the substitution of a pattern for a reading.
